LOO information criteria for mvgam models

Source: R/loo.mvgam.R
loo.mvgam.Rd

Extract the LOOIC (leave-one-out information criterion) using loo::loo().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
loo(
  x,
  ...,
  compare = TRUE,
  resp = NULL,
  pointwise = FALSE,
  moment_match = FALSE,
  reloo = FALSE,
  k_threshold = 0.7,
  save_psis = FALSE,
  moment_match_args = list(),
  reloo_args = list(),
  model_names = NULL,
  incl_autocor = TRUE,
  incl_dynamics = NULL,
  by_series = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
loo_compare(
  x,
  ...,
  criterion = c("loo", "waic"),
  model_names = NULL,
  incl_autocor = TRUE,
  incl_dynamics = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A fitted mvgam or jsdgam object.

...

For loo(), further arguments to loo::loo(). For loo_compare(), further fitted models.

compare, resp, pointwise, moment_match, reloo, k_threshold, save_psis, moment_match_args, reloo_args

The arguments of brms::loo.brmsfit. mvgam uses two of them. resp scopes a multivariate fit to one response. save_psis keeps the smoothing object. pointwise would stream the density. moment_match and reloo would refit the model, configured by k_threshold and the *_args lists. compare and model_names would rank several models, which loo_compare.mvgam() does. mvgam runs none of these. Supplying one raises an error naming it.

model_names

Character vector of row names for the comparison, one per model. NULL takes them from the call.

incl_autocor

Logical, default TRUE. Passed to log_lik.mvgam(). TRUE scores each observation under the latent trend state the model inferred at that time. The ELPD then describes the series that was observed. FALSE scores the deterministic submodel alone.

incl_dynamics

Deprecated alias for incl_autocor.

by_series

Logical, default FALSE. TRUE returns a data frame with one row per series and columns series, elpd, se_elpd, p and n_obs, as spOccupancy::waicOcc(by.sp = TRUE) ranks species. An occupancy or N-mixture fit is scored per site, each site counted in its species.

criterion

"loo" (the default) or "waic".

Value

For loo.mvgam, an object of class psis_loo (see loo::loo()). For loo_compare.mvgam, the compare.loo table of loo::loo_compare(), one row per model, best first. Its p_worse, diag_diff and diag_elpd columns follow Sivula et al. (2025).

Details

When comparing two (or more) fitted mvgam models, we can estimate the difference in their in-sample predictive accuracies using the Expected Log Predictive Density (ELPD). This metric can be approximated using Pareto Smoothed Importance Sampling (PSIS), which re-weights posterior draws to approximate predictions for a datapoint had it not been included in the original model fit (i.e. leave-one-out cross-validation).

See loo::loo() and loo::loo_compare() for further details on how this importance sampling works.

A fit with a latent trend routinely strains this approximation. Leaving an observation out keeps its influence on the state the model inferred at that time. The re-weighted density still conditions on a state estimated from that observation. The ELPD then measures conditional in-sample fit. The effective number of parameters climbs towards the number of observations. Check the Pareto \(k\) diagnostics before trusting a comparison. lfo_cv.mvgam() refits along the time axis and scores each window against data the model has not seen. forecast.mvgam() with score.mvgam_forecast() scores a held-out horizon.

References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A. and Gabry, J. (2017). Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Statistics and Computing, 27:1413-1432. doi:10.1007/s11222-016-9696-4

Burkner, P.-C., Gabry, J. and Vehtari, A. (2020). Approximate leave-future-out cross-validation for Bayesian time series models. Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation, 90(14):2499-2523. doi:10.1080/00949655.2020.1783262

Sivula, T., Magnusson, M., Matamoros, A. A. and Vehtari, A. (2025). Uncertainty in Bayesian leave-one-out cross-validation based model comparison. Bayesian Analysis. doi:10.1214/25-BA1569

See also

lfo_cv.mvgam() scores forecasts by refitting along the time axis. kfold.mvgam() runs grouped k-fold cross-validation. loo_model_weights.mvgam() weights models by their predictions. The forecast evaluation article compares models by approximate and exact cross-validation.

Other model comparison: bridge_sampler.mvgam(), compare_elpds(), kfold.mvgam(), lfo_cv.mvgam(), log_lik.mvgam(), loo_compare.mvgam_lfo(), mvgam_loo_extras, posterior_average.mvgam(), waic.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
# A Poisson GAM without a latent trend. PSIS approximates each
# held-out count of such a model well (see Details of ?loo.mvgam)
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = "None")
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), data = simdat$data_train,
             family = poisson(), chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 2 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
# }
# \dontrun{
# The same smooth of x replaced by a linear effect
mod_lin <- update(mod, formula. = y ~ x)

# The ELPD estimate, with Pareto k diagnostics for each observation
loo(mod)
#> 
#> Computed from 2000 posterior draws and 90 log-likelihood terms.
#> 
#>          Estimate   SE
#> elpd_loo   -208.8  8.5
#> p_loo         8.0  1.5
#> looic       417.7 17.0
#> ------
#> MCSE of elpd_loo is 0.1.
#> MCSE and ESS estimates assume MCMC draws (r_eff in [0.4, 1.2]).
#> 
#> All Pareto k estimates are good (k < 0.7).
#> See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.

# The better model comes first, with elpd_diff = 0. The diagnostic
# columns say how far the difference can be trusted
loo_compare(mod, mod_lin)
#>    model elpd_diff se_diff p_worse diag_diff diag_elpd
#>      mod       0.0     0.0      NA                    
#>  mod_lin     -26.1     9.7    1.00   N < 100          
#> 
#> Diagnostic flags present.
#> See ?`loo-glossary` (sections `diag_diff` and `diag_elpd`)
#> or https://mc-stan.org/loo/reference/loo-glossary.html.

# Next: lfo_cv() scores each model's forecasts of data it has not
# seen
# }
